summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem has matured into the standard way AI agents connect to external tools, data sources, and services through a uniform JSON-RPC interface. By 2026, it spans three layers: aggregator platforms that bundle thousands of integrations behind one endpoint, gateways that secure and proxy MCP traffic, and individual servers that expose a single service like browser automation or a GitHub repo. This matters because MCP eliminates custom glue code, letting agents discover and invoke real-world capabilities securely and at scale.
ecosystem_note: Aggregators expose many services through one managed endpoint, gateways sit in front of MCP servers to handle auth/security/routing, and individual servers each wrap a single tool or service.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.connects_to: Browser automation and web scraping — lets LLMs navigate, click, fill forms, and extract data from web pages via structured accessibility snapshots
strengths: Highest search volume of any MCP server (~35,000/mo)
tools.best_for: Agent-driven browser automation, end-to-end testing, and web data extraction

tools.name: Composio
tools.connects_to: 1,500+ apps (GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Notion, databases) through a single managed MCP endpoint with a self-learning tool-selection layer
tools.pricing_paid: Usage-based paid tiers for higher volume and enterprise features
strengths: 1B+ tool calls run on the platform
Self-improving layer: repeat tasks run 30% more accurately on 2× fewer tokens
tools.best_for: Teams wanting one managed endpoint across hundreds of SaaS apps without per-tool setup

tools.name: Figma MCP
tools.connects_to: Design files — lets agents read Figma layers, components, and styles to generate code or extract design context
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Figma plans; free tier available
tools.best_for: Design-to-code generation and pulling design context into coding agents

tools.name: GitHub MCP
tools.connects_to: GitHub repos — issues, PRs, code, Actions; enables repo automation, triage, and CI workflows
tools.pricing_paid: Included with GitHub plans; free tier available
strengths: OAuth-secured remote server, works in CI environments
Backed by GitHub/Microsoft with frequent updates
tools.best_for: Repo automation, issue triage, and CI/CD workflows inside coding agents

tools.name: Context7
tools.connects_to: Up-to-date library and framework documentation injected into agent context on demand
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid Upstash plans for higher usage
strengths: Remote server, reduces hallucinated/outdated API usage
Popular with coding agents like Cursor
tools.best_for: Feeding current, version-accurate docs into coding assistants

tools.name: Supabase MCP
tools.connects_to: Postgres databases, auth, and storage — lets agents query and manage Supabase projects
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Supabase plans; free tier available
strengths: Full database + backend access for agents
tools.best_for: Agents that need to read/write application databases and backend services

tools.name: Notion MCP
tools.connects_to: Notion workspaces — pages, databases, and docs for reading and writing knowledge content
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Notion plans; free tier available
strengths: Strong for knowledge management and documentation agents
tools.best_for: Knowledge-base automation and docs/notes management by agents

tools.name: n8n MCP
tools.connects_to: Workflow automation — triggers and runs n8n workflows spanning 400+ integrations from an agent
tools.pricing_paid: Cloud paid plans; self-hosted free (fair-code license)
strengths: Connects agents to large library of workflow automations
tools.best_for: Bridging AI agents into existing automation workflows and multi-step pipelines

tools.name: Zapier MCP
tools.connects_to: 7,000+ apps through Zapier's automation platform exposed as MCP tools
tools.pricing_paid: Zapier paid plans for higher task volume and premium apps
strengths: Massive app catalog with no-code setup
tools.best_for: Instant access to thousands of SaaS integrations without custom servers

tools.name: Jira MCP
tools.connects_to: Jira issues, projects, and sprints — lets agents create, query, and update tickets
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Atlassian/Jira plans; free tier available
tools.best_for: Automating issue tracking, sprint management, and dev project workflows

tools.name: Slack MCP
tools.connects_to: Slack channels and messages — lets agents read, post, and summarize conversations
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Slack plans; free tier available
strengths: Common target for notification and standup automations
tools.best_for: Agents posting updates, summaries, and alerts into team channels

tools.name: AWS MCP
tools.connects_to: AWS services and billing — lets agents query infrastructure, costs, and resources
tools.pricing_paid: AWS usage-based pricing for underlying services
strengths: Covers billing and infra workflows for platform engineers
tools.best_for: Cloud infrastructure management and cost analysis by agents
